searchDocs.title: Wave​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Wave { wavelength: number-- Studs between crests amplitude: number-- Crest height in studs steepness: number-- 0..1; 0 = pure sine swell, 1 = sharpest allowed direction: Vector2 -- Travel direction; need not be normalised } A single wave definition

searchDocs.title: Prepared​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Prepared { waves: {PreparedWave}-- Precomputed constants, one per input wave steepness: number-- Average steepness across all waves, 0..1 } Precomputed wave data returned by Gerstner.prepare

searchDocs.title: prepare​
searchDocs.content: </> Gerstner.prepare( waves: {Wave}-- The wave definitions to prepare ) → Prepared-- Precomputed waves plus the average steepness Validates a wave set once and precomputes every wave constant

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"needs at least one wave"	Raised when 'waves' is empty

searchDocs.title: displace​
searchDocs.content: </> Gerstner.displace( prepared: Prepared,-- The result of Gerstner.prepare x: number,-- Rest position X in studs z: number,-- Rest position Z in studs t: number-- Time in seconds ) → Vector3 -- Absolute displaced position Returns the absolute world position of the surface point whose rest position is '(x, z)'. 'y' is relative to the water plane's own level; the renderer adds sea level

searchDocs.title: Prepare once, displace a lot​
searchDocs.content: prepare validates your wave set and precomputes every per wave const, so the hot loop never calls sqrt  local gerstner = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.gerstner) local prepared = gerstner.prepare({ { wavelength = 40, amplitude = 2, steepness = 0.5, direction = Vector2.new(1, 0) }, { wavelength = 70, amplitude = 3, steepness = 0.4, direction = Vector2.new(0.7, 0.7) }, })

searchDocs.title: Sampling the surface​
searchDocs.content: local position = gerstner.displace(prepared, x, z, t) -- position.Y is relative to the water plane, not to sea level

searchDocs.title: Verifying it works​
searchDocs.content: One wave - wavelength = 40, amplitude = 2, steepness = 0.5, direction = Vector2.new(1, 0), t = 0 - reproduces this exactly:  x	.Y	.X0	0	3.183 10	+2	10 20	0	16.817 30	-2	30 40	0	43.183 50	+2	50  The .X column is not decoration, Gerstner displaces X and Z as well as Y, which is what bunches crests and stretches troughs. That term is zero at a crest or a trough, and maximal at the zero crossing, so X == x at x = 10 is correct, not a dead term

searchDocs.title: Fail fast​
searchDocs.content: prepare throws at setup time and names the offending wave, since it rejects a wavelength <= 0 an amplitude <= 0 (Q divides by amplitude, so zero would produce infinite positions), a steepness outside 0..1 (above 1 the wave self intersects and the surface spikes), a zero length direction, and an empty wave list

searchDocs.title: Performance​
searchDocs.content: displace costs a handful of multiplies and two trig calls per wave, so reuse a single prepared value and write vertices in one batch, per vertex SetPosition in a loop is a known trap!

searchDocs.title: Before you start​
searchDocs.content: This must run on the client! EditableMesh does not replicate, a server built mesh renders on the server ONLY. The client receives an unusable Object, put the script in a LocalScript

searchDocs.title: The script​
searchDocs.content: --!strict local AssetService = game:GetService("AssetService") local RuNService = game:GetService("RunService") local gerstner = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.gerstner) local GRID_SEGMENTS = 64 -- (N+1)^2 = 4.225 verts, 2N^2 = 8.192 tris (cap 20K) local PLANE_SIZE = 512 -- cellSize 8: all three waves validated at this rate local SEA_LEVEL = 0 const WAVES = { { wavelength = 40, amplitude = 1, steepness = 0.8, direction = Vector2.new(1, 0) }, { wavelength = 70, amplitude = 2, steepness = 0.75, direction = Vector2.new(0.7, 0.7) }, { wavelength = 120, amplitude = 1, steepness = 0.7, direction = Vector2.new(-0.4, 0.9) }, } local prepared = gerstner.prepare(WAVES) const cellSize = PLANE_SIZE / GRID_SEGMENTS const half = PLANE_SIZE / 2 const rowLength = GRID_SEGMENTS + 1 const vertexCount = rowLength * rowLength local mesh = AssetService:CreateEditableMesh() const vertexIds = table.create(vertexCount) const restX = table.create(vertexCount) const restZ = table.create(vertexCount) -- flat rest grid in LOCAL coords, indexed so neighbours share verts: that is what gives smooth shading and keeps the triangle budget for iz = 0, GRID_SEGMENTS do for ix = 0, GRID_SEGMENTS do const lx = -half + ix * cellSize const lz = -half + iz * cellSize const index = iz * rowLength + ix + 1 restX[index] = lx restZ[index] = lz vertexIds[index] = mesh:AddVertex(Vector3.new(lx, 0, lz)) end end local function writeVertices(t: number, originX: number, originZ: number) const positions = table.create(vertexCount) for i = 1, vertexCount do -- sample at world XZ, never local, or the surface drags with the camera const worldX = originX + restX[i] const worldZ = originZ + restZ[i] const p = gerstner.displace(prepared, worldX, worldZ, t) -- displace() returns an ABSOLUTE world position, so subtract origin for local space positions[i] = Vector3.new(p.X - originX, p.Y, p.Z - originZ) end mesh:BatchSetValues(vertexIds, positions) end -- displace before adding faces, so each normal normal comes from the waved positions writeVertices(0, 0, 0) -- quads wound {v00, v10, v11, v01}: up facing normals for iz = 0, GRID_SEGMENTS - 1 do for ix = 0, GRID_SEGMENTS - 1 do const v00 = iz * rowLength + ix + 1 const v01 = v00 + 1 const v10 = v00 + rowLength const v11 = v10 + 1 mesh:AddFace({ vertexIds[v00], vertexIds[v10], vertexIds[v11], vertexIds[v01] }) end end local part = AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(Content.fromObject(mesh)) part.Anchored = true part.CFrame = CFrame.new(0, SEA_LEVEL, 0) part.CanCollide = false part.CanQuery = false part.CanTouch = false part.CastShadow = false part.Parent = workspace const camera = workspace.CurrentCamera const startClock = os.clock() RuNService.Heartbeat:Connect(function() const t = os.clock() - startClock -- snaap the window to grid step so neighbouring nodes keep exact heights as it movees, no popping, crawling gand world stable UVs later const originX = math.floor(camera.CFrame.Position.X / cellSize) * cellSize const originZ = math.floor(camera.CFrame.Position.Z / cellSize) * cellSize -- so origins move the part and then write, vertex local coords depend on the origin part.CFrame = CFrame.new(originX, SEA_LEVEL, originZ) writeVertices(t, originX, originZ) end)
